children: Japanese rubber futures fell for a third consecutive session on Friday on profit-taking after a short squeeze and arbitrage-driven rally this week, although the contract still posted a weekly gain as higher oil prices capped losses.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for February delivery
was down 2.9 yen, or 0.67%, to close at 431 yen ($2.80) per kg.
The contract, however, gained 1.38% this week.
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
fell 285 yuan, or 1.45%, to 19,315 yuan ($2,879.10) per metric ton.
The most active October butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) lost 560 yuan, or 3.53%, to 15,295 yuan per metric ton.

The market diverged from fundamentals during the rally, and current declines are largely a result of funds taking profit after a squeeze on short positions and arbitrage players, a Singapore-based trader said.
The market is expected to enter a consolidation phase before adjusting back toward fundamentals, said the trader.
slumped on Friday on renewed concerns over U.S. rate hikes and a surge in oil prices that fuelled inflation worries.

Oil prices fell, but both major benchmarks are on track to end the week above $100 a barrel for the first time since mid-May, as increasing attacks along key shipping routes in the Middle East fuel fears of a prolonged disruption to supplies.
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil.
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for November delivery (STFX6) last traded at 242.2 U.S. cents per kg, down 0.9%, as of 0700 GMT.
